title: Lakehouse: iceberg-pg catalog-DB failover is graceful N/A (actionable)
description: Runs `nexus failover-test cluster lakehouse --direction iceberg-pg --yes`. The catalog-DB failover is a graceful actionable N/A (diagnosed live in v0.8.4): a keepalived VRRP cutover of the .151 VIP is not a safe one-shot — the notify_master hook promotes the standby while nopreempt leaves the old primary un-demoted (split-brain), and the promoted standby pg_hba does not admit the Nessie REST hosts, so the catalog front door lands on a PG Nessie cannot use. A real catalog-DB failover is a DR runbook (promote + demote/fence + pg_basebackup re-seed). The verb refuses with the full explanation and points at the spark-master direction.

observe.what: an actionable N/A: the VRRP cutover promotes the standby into a split-brain + the pg_hba/Nessie mismatch; use --direction spark-master for the live-proven failover

whatProves: LakehouseAdapter.FailoverAsync graceful-N/As the iceberg-pg direction — a keepalived VRRP cutover of a PG primary/standby pair is unsafe as an adapter one-shot (split-brain + pg_hba), so the verb explains why and routes to the spark-master HA drill.
